VERDICT: the guard FIX-NUMCONV removes can never fail on this build, and removing it changes no value. Full argument: C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/numconv/argue/argument.md (md5 3b5e8448).

THE FACT. The removed guard is the result guard's round trip, cvttsd2si(cvtsi2sd(y)) == y, where y is the operand's own CONV i64.num. The x64 backend compiles every unguarded CONV i64.num to `cvttsd2si r64, xmm/m64` [S: asm_conv, lj_asm_x86.h ~:900-931]. The backend has no FP-to-int instruction that rounds by MXCSR: lj_target_x86.h defines XO_CVTTSD2SI and no XO_CVTSD2SI [S]. So y is either the double's integral part (any double in [-2^63, 2^63)) or INT64_MIN. Each of those is an integer that is exactly a double. cvtsi2sd of y is therefore exact in every rounding mode, and truncating it back gives y [S][I]. Two measurements back this:
- CPU probe: 21.18M doubles in each of 8 MXCSR settings (RN/RD/RU/RZ, with DAZ+FTZ off and on) gave 0 mismatches, and y was exact every time. The fail-first controls do fail, e.g. 2^53+1 and INT64_MAX [M: runs/cvt-rt-1].
- In the build: identity loops over boundary values had exactly one trace exit each (the loop end). A control that does fail its guard had 28 exits [M: runs/exits-ident-2].

THE CONSTANT FOLD. kfold_conv_knum_i64_num computes INT64FOLD((uint64_t)lj_num2i64(k)). On x64, lj_num2i64 is the DynASM routine lj_vm_num2i64, which is just `cvttsd2si rax, xmm0; ret`. There is no C float-to-int conversion, so no undefined behaviour [S]. objdump of the shipped lj_opt_fold.o (1d018acc) shows `call lj_vm_num2i64`, and lj_vm.o (583d6da3) holds `f2 48 0f 2c c0 cvttsd2si; ret`. So the fold and the trace run the same instruction [M]. The fold is reachable in the loop copy (`v | 0; v = C` with C a literal), and its values equal -joff [M: runs/kfold-copy-1, kfold-copy-dump-1].

EMITTERS. Only oclj_rec_bitarg (op2 0x12ae), the result guard's own back-conversion (0x16ae, ANY|EXACT) and their loop copies produce CONV i64.num. None is guarded, and all are typed i64 [S]. Every upstream emitter is ruled out: FFI-only, hunk 8, no XSTORE without FFI, a no-op SPLIT, or source modes that are only NUM_INT/INT_NUM [S]. Measured over 14 loop shapes: only 0x12ae and 0x16ae appear [M: runs/modes-2].

WHEN IT FIRES. back becomes res, and comm_equal drops `EQ.i64 res, res`. back has no other consumer, and snapshots name only d. A dropped guard leaves J->guardemit unset, so a snapshot that no guard uses may merge; that is upstream's own mechanism [S]. Across PHIs:
- The rule returns an existing ref of type I64, which meets requirement 2 and S4.
- It reads only y's opcode, type and literal mode, which meets S5.
- When fleft is PHI-marked, y is already the copy's res and is already PHI-marked, so the rule adds no PHI [S][I].

SHAPES. On the base build each of 11 identity forms has 1 i64 EQ guard in the pre-roll and 1 in the body; the 4 cancellation forms have 2 [M: runs/ir-ident-1]. The cancellations are ~~x, (x~y)~y, (x~5)~5 and ~(x~-1). Their inner guards must stay: ~x of an exact x >= 2^53 with bit 0 clear is inexact and raises, as 5.3.6 does [M: runs/vals-ident-1]. JIT output equals -joff on boundary values, invalid values included [M: runs/vals-ident-2].

x64 ONLY. arm64's FCVTZS saturates to INT64_MAX, which is not a double, so this argument does not port [S]. Side finding: on arm64, round 3's operand guard would also accept x = 2^63 [I]. arm64 is parked, so this is moot for now.

verify-rg2's DIFF is sound on this build but not shippable as written [S]. Merged into the width rule's line, it removes the text `<= 54)`. Two things depend on that text: patch-bitop-fold.sh verify_content (:434, :439) and negctl's WIDTH55 arm anchor (:733-735). Step 2 should give the rule its own line.

PROPOSED ARMS for step 2:
- NUMCONVOP1: the rule fires for a bit operator whose op1 is a converted double. Written memory-safe.
- NUMCONVW: oclj_bitwidth scores a converted double as 54. This is the exactness-versus-range trap.
- NUMCONVOFF: the rule switched off. Only an IR count can catch it.

The catching case for the first two is probes/catch_numconv.lua. It meets 2^53 | 1 and similar in the same compiled loop that was recorded on small values. On base, 7 forms raise 300/300 in 8 option sets, all equal to -joff [M: runs/catch-numconv-4]. Under either arm the trace would return the rounded double instead [I].

report.summary:
I built FIX-NUMCONV and verified it in a scratch copy of 209aa95; the repo was not touched. Of all 80 objects, only `lj_opt_fold.o` differs from build/native's. On every trace I dumped, the fold removes only the result guard of an identity operation and changes nothing else. All three runners pass. The timing chain is written and smoke-run, but the full chain has not been run.

**What changed, and the rule** [S]
- Two files in the copy changed; `build-native.sh` is unchanged.
- The new check is `oclj_isnumconv` in `oclj_bitop_fold.c`, next to `oclj_bitwidth`. It is true when y is an unguarded CONV i64.num of a double: `ir->o == IR_CONV && irt_isi64(ir->t) && !irt_isguard(ir->t) && (ir->op2 & IRCONV_SRCMASK) == IRT_NUM`.
- Hunk 7 calls it right after the width rule, inside the block that already handles PHIs (fix1), before upstream's PHIBARRIER: `if (oclj_isnumconv(J, fleft->op1)) return fleft->op1;`.
- Why the removed guard cannot fail:
  - For that IR, x64's `asm_conv` (lj_asm_x86.h:900-931 at the pin) emits exactly one `cvttsd2si r64`. The result is the double's integral part, or -2^63 for NaN, infinities and out-of-range values. Each of those is exactly a double, so converting to double and back gives y.
  - A constant x never reaches the rule as a CONV: `kfold_conv_knum_i64_num` (lj_opt_fold.c:901-905) folds it to a KINT64 using `lj_vm_num2i64`, which is the same `cvttsd2si` (vm_x64.dasc:2684-2686).
- Why only I64, never U64: a u64 conversion adds -2^64 and converts again (:911-925), and returning a u64-typed value would change the folded instruction's type. A grep finds no CONV u64.num emitted outside FFI code.
- Bits the check ignores: the check mode, SEXT and the exact mark, because `asm_conv` ignores them for this conversion.
- I made the function `static LJ_AINLINE` so `bitop_wgate.c`, and with it `build-native.sh`, needs no change. The -Wall -Wextra gate still parses the uncalled function: a planted sign-compare in it raised one warning [M, proto/wgate].

**Patch script** [M]
- NADD is now 70 (63 + 7); NDEL stays 8.
- New checks in `verify_content`: `oclj_isnumconv(` appears on exactly one line, the call is on `fleft->op1`, and it sits between the width rule's call and the PHIBARRIER.
- The script has no CR, tab or backslash, and its hunk engine block is unchanged (`077d1dbebe05`).
- Fail-first, `proto/ff-patch-2`: 10 of 10 cases behaved as expected. A stray line in the input fails the count check alone. Edits to the hunk text are caught by the count, the call text and the order check. HEAD's NADD fails the line count. HEAD's script still reproduces b0's patched file.

- `ident.lua`: in each of the five loop traces (or0, andm1, xor0, shl0, shr0), one result-guard pair disappears in the pre-roll and one in the loop body. With the opcode test gone, any int64 operator whose op2 has low five bits equal to 14 loses its result guard, and that includes an op2 that refers to another instruction, not just to a constant [M verify-arm/irscan-1].
